title: Microsoft 365 Outage Rolls Into Second Day, Knocking Out Indian Airlines' Email Support
excerpt: Outlook and Exchange Online have been failing worldwide since Thursday evening. IndiGo and Akasa Air warned passengers their email support is down, Air India rerouted its mail, and Microsoft — reporting only 'marginal success' by Friday afternoon — has given no time for full recovery.
body:
• A worldwide Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday evening left Exchange Online and Outlook mailboxes failing into Friday, with Microsoft reporting only "marginal success" in restoring service by Friday afternoon India time.
  • IndiGo told passengers its email support is impacted and it may not receive their emails; Akasa Air reported delays and pointed customers to its 24/7 care centre.
  • Air India said its flights were unaffected and that it had temporarily rerouted its email, still answering within its usual 24 hours.
  • If you are waiting on an airline reply by email, use the app, website assistant or phone instead — Microsoft has reported delays, not loss of mail, and queued messages should arrive once mailboxes recover.

If Outlook would not open for you on Friday morning, it was not your laptop. Microsoft 365 has been in a worldwide outage since the evening of Thursday, November 12, and for Indian offices and airlines it ran straight into Friday's working day, taking down the email support desks of two of the country's biggest carriers.

IndiGo, India's largest airline, told customers: "Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails." The airline directed passengers needing urgent help to 6E Skai, its assistant on its website and mobile app, and said its other support channels remained available. Akasa Air issued a similar warning of delays to its email support and directed passengers to its 24/7 Akasa Care Centre and social media channels. Air India took a different route: it said its flight operations and communication channels were unaffected, that it had temporarily rerouted its emails so messages continue to reach it, and that it was responding within its usual 24-hour timeline.

What broke

The incident centres on Exchange Online, the system behind Outlook mailboxes. Microsoft's updates, as tracked by KeyXplore's timeline of the incident, describe large numbers of servers becoming unavailable, restarted servers failing automated health checks and being pulled from service, and servers that were brought back becoming unresponsive again once they began receiving traffic. Microsoft began reverting a recent network configuration change that correlates with the start of the impact, later said that change was "not taking as expected," and by 12:27 p.m. IST on Friday reported only that "we have observed marginal success." The incident references for administrators are EX1550543 (Exchange Online) and MO1550821 (Microsoft 365).

"We have observed marginal success."

— Microsoft incident update, 12:27 p.m. IST, November 13

Microsoft has said there is no indication the outage is the result of malicious activity, and that the extra load is not explained by a rise in user traffic. It has not named a root cause and has given no time for full recovery. Complaint tracker Downdetector logged roughly 130,000 to 140,000 Outlook problem reports worldwide at the peak, including about 2,157 reports from India late on Thursday night — user reports, not a count of affected accounts. Teams chat and meetings were mostly working, though calendars and scheduling could fail, and features in Copilot, SharePoint and other apps that depend on a mailbox or calendar were also affected. The outage is a Microsoft 365 incident; Microsoft's incident does not list Azure.

What travellers and workers should do

The damage so far is to email, not to flying: the airlines' advisories concern support inboxes, and Air India stated explicitly that flight operations were unaffected. Passengers with an urgent issue should not rely on email today — use the airline's app or website assistant, or phone. For office workers, the practical advice from incident trackers is to leave Outlook profiles and passwords alone, since the fault is on Microsoft's side; queued mail should arrive once a mailbox is reachable again. Microsoft's public status page is at status.cloud.microsoft, and administrators can follow service health in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

What happens next

Recovery has been partial and uneven, and Microsoft itself has said its actions are not yet producing sustained recovery. The pattern to watch is whether restarted servers stay up once real traffic returns. Microsoft has promised a post-incident report once service is restored, which is where the confirmed cause will appear.
